senses.gloss:
Śākhā in the Rigveda and later denotes the ‘branch’ of a tree. vayā is more often used in this sense in the Rigveda.
Foot notes i. 8, 8; vii. 43, 1; x. 94, 3.
Av. iii. 6, 8; x. 7, 21; xi. 2, 19, etc.

Sakhi, ‘friend,’ is common from the Rigveda onwards, both literally and metaphorically.
Foot notes i. 164, 20 (of birds); iii. 43, 4 (of steeds); ii. 1, 9; v. 12, 5; vi. 75, 3, etc.
Av. v. 4, 7; 11, 9; 13, 5, etc. So sakhitva and sakhya, ‘friendship,’ are also common--e.g., Rv. i. 10, 6; iii. 1, 15; iv. 25, 2, etc., and Rv. 1. 178, 2; ii. 18, 8; vii. 22, 9, etc.
